evidence_note: Identity problem: the cited 2024 work is a multitask multimodal machine-unlearning benchmark, not the 2025 multilingual MuBench (61 languages, arXiv:2506.19468); coded from the cited paper, whose documentation does not establish multilingual language coverage, so languages, origin, tier and cultural specificity left undetermined.

canonical_reference: Winogrande: An Adversarial Winograd Schema Challenge at Scale. arXiv:1907.10641 (2019).
evidence_note: English-only benchmark of crowdsourced Winograd-style commonsense problems authored in English (44k problems); a monolingual resource with no explicit tier characterization in the source.

canonical_reference: SeaEval: Benchmarking Multilingual Foundation Models. arXiv:2309.04766.
languages: Chinese; English; Filipino; Indonesian; Malay; Singlish; Spanish; Vietnamese
evidence_note: Suite of 29 datasets (13,263 samples) across 8 languages including Singlish, including newly constructed cultural-understanding datasets for the US, Singapore, China and the Philippines; it aggregates existing and newly constructed datasets and the majority data-origin composition is not established in the sources consulted, so origin and tier left undetermined.

canonical_reference: M3Exam: A Multilingual, Multimodal and Multi-level Benchmark for Examining Large Language Models. arXiv:2306.05179.
evidence_note: Built from real school exam papers originally written in each language, with a multimodal subset; language count reported as 9 in the sources consulted, which do not enumerate the full language list.

Vision-language QA benchmark over culturally diverse images from 73 countries covering 100 languages (22.7K QA); questions produced via GPT-4o translation human-verified and corrected by native experts; language list not enumerated in the sources consulted.

canonical_reference: SEACrowd: A Multilingual Multimodal Data Hub and Benchmark Suite for Southeast Asian Languages. arXiv:2406.10118.
evidence_note: Benchmarks in the catalogue cover 36 indigenous Southeast Asian languages across 13 tasks (the wider catalogue spans nearly 1,000 SEA languages); constituent datasets are existing resources originally in the local languages; multi-task catalogue, coded Other.

canonical_reference: Conneau et al. (2018), XNLI: Evaluating Cross-lingual Sentence Representations. EMNLP 2018. arXiv:1809.05053.
languages: Arabic; Bulgarian; Chinese; English; French; German; Greek; Hindi; Russian; Spanish; Swahili; Thai; Turkish; Urdu; Vietnamese
evidence_note: MultiNLI development and test sets human-translated into 15 languages; the paper names Swahili and Urdu as low-resource while the remaining languages are higher-resource, so no single tier coded.

canonical_reference: IndicXNLI. arXiv:2204.08776 (2022).
evidence_note: English XNLI machine-translated (IndicTrans) into 11 Indic languages; the 11 languages are not enumerated by name in the sources consulted.

canonical_reference: FarsTail: A Persian Natural Language Inference Dataset. arXiv:2009.08820 (2020).
evidence_note: Persian NLI dataset of 10,367 samples generated natively from 3,539 Persian multiple-choice questions; a monolingual resource with no explicit tier characterization in the source.

canonical_reference: AmericasNLI. arXiv:2104.08726 (2021).
languages: Asháninka; Aymara; Bribri; Guaraní; Nahuatl; Otomí; Quechua; Rarámuri; Shipibo-Konibo; Wixarika
evidence_note: XNLI subset translated from the Spanish version into 10 Indigenous languages of the Americas, characterized in the source as truly low-resource languages.

canonical_reference: BasqueGLUE. LREC 2022 (ACL Anthology 2022.lrec-1.172).
evidence_note: Basque NLU benchmark elaborated from previously existing Basque datasets; the source calls Basque a less-resourced language, coded Low.

canonical_reference: Kakwani et al. (2020), IndicGLUE (IndicNLP Suite).
languages: Assamese; Bengali; Gujarati; Hindi; Kannada; Malayalam; Marathi; Odia; Punjabi; Tamil; Telugu
evidence_note: NLU suite spanning news classification, headline prediction, Wikipedia section-title prediction, multiple-choice QA, NER and cross-lingual sentence retrieval across 11 Indic languages; sources consulted do not establish a majority native/translated composition, so origin and tier left undetermined.

canonical_reference: Doddapaneni et al. (2023), Towards Leaving No Indic Language Behind. ACL 2023 (2023.acl-long.693).
evidence_note: Human-supervised benchmark of 105 test sets over 9 NLU tasks covering 20 Indic languages; it combines translated English benchmark sets with curated in-language datasets (52 of the sets are new), so origin coded Mixed.

canonical_reference: Timilsina et al. (2022), NepBERTa / Nep-gLUE. LREC 2022.
evidence_note: First Nepali NLU benchmark (Timilsina et al., 2022) with 4 tasks (NER, POS tagging, content classification, categorical pair similarity) built on Nepali data; Nepali is characterized as a low-resource language in the source literature; roster year is 2025 while the introducing paper is from LREC 2022.

canonical_reference: Zhang, Ouni & Eger, Cross-lingual Cross-temporal Summarization: Dataset, Models, Evaluation. arXiv:2306.12916.
evidence_note: First cross-lingual cross-temporal summarization corpus (328 hDe-En and 289 hEn-De instances) built from historical fiction texts and Wikipedia summaries originally in English and German; pairs are not produced by translation.

canonical_reference: Perez-Beltrachini & Lapata (2021), Models and Datasets for Cross-Lingual Summarisation. EMNLP 2021.
evidence_note: Cross-lingual summarization corpus derived from Wikipedia in four European languages (Czech, English, French, German) across twelve language pairs; document-summary pairs formed via interlanguage links with the lead section as summary, not by translation; roster year 2022, paper EMNLP 2021.

canonical_reference: Zhang & Eickhoff, CroCoSum: A Benchmark Dataset for Cross-Lingual Code-Switched Summarization. arXiv:2303.04092.
evidence_note: Over 24,000 English technology-news articles paired with over 18,000 naturally occurring human-written Chinese-English code-switched summaries collected from Solidot; summaries were not produced by translation for this dataset.

canonical_reference: Ladhak et al. (2020), WikiLingua: A New Benchmark Dataset for Cross-Lingual Abstractive Summarization. EMNLP 2020 Findings. arXiv:2010.03093.
languages: Arabic; Chinese; Czech; Dutch; English; French; German; Hindi; Indonesian; Italian; Japanese; Korean; Portuguese; Russian; Spanish; Thai; Turkish; Vietnamese
evidence_note: Article-summary pairs in 18 languages extracted from WikiHow guides human-authored in each language; gold cross-lingual alignments created via the images used for each how-to step, not by translation.

canonical_reference: Shi et al. (2022), Language Models are Multilingual Chain-of-Thought Reasoners (MGSM).
languages: Bengali; Chinese; English; French; German; Japanese; Russian; Spanish; Swahili; Telugu; Thai
evidence_note: First 250 GSM8K problems, originally written in English, translated into 10 further languages (11 total); the source categorization splits the set into high-resource (en, zh, fr, de, ja, ru, es) and low-resource (bn, th, te, sw) languages, so no single tier coded.

canonical_reference: Son et al. (2025), Linguistic Generalizability of Test-Time Scaling in Mathematical Reasoning. ACL 2025. arXiv:2502.17407.
evidence_note: Competition-level math benchmark covering 55 languages in four subsets: MATH-500 and AIME subsets machine-translated with GPT-4o, plus human-translated/official IMO translations and natively sourced regional olympiad problems, so origin coded Mixed; language list not enumerated in the sources consulted.

canonical_reference: Liu et al. (2025), MaXIFE: Multilingual and Cross-lingual Instruction Following Evaluation. ACL 2025.
evidence_note: 1,667 verifiable instruction tasks built from 795 base questions as parallel prompts across 23 languages, produced through a translation phase with human translation processes for questions and instructions; primary class is instruction following, which has no class of its own and is coded Other.

canonical_reference: Liu et al. (2025), XRAG: Cross-lingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation. arXiv:2505.10089.
evidence_note: Cross-document Q&A pairs generated in English from news article pairs, quality-controlled, then human-translated into German, Spanish, Chinese and Arabic for monolingual-retrieval and multilingual-retrieval settings.

canonical_reference: Raihan, Anastasopoulos & Zampieri (2025), mHumanEval — A Multilingual Benchmark to Evaluate Large Language Models for Code Generation. NAACL 2025.
evidence_note: Code-generation benchmark with prompts in 204 natural languages compiled using established machine translation with quality assurance, plus expert human translations for 15 languages; the full language list is not enumerated in the sources consulted and no single tier is characterized for the set.

canonical_reference: CL-HumanEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-Lingual Transfer through Code Generation. PACLIC 2024.
evidence_note: HumanEval-structured dataset (version 1) generated using GPT-4o mini, with the Japanese docstrings produced by LLM translation of the English ones, built to evaluate English-Japanese cross-lingual transfer in code generation.

canonical_reference: Doddapaneni et al. (2024), Cross-Lingual Auto Evaluation for Assessing Multilingual LLMs. arXiv:2410.13394.
languages: Bengali; French; German; Hindi; Telugu; Urdu
evidence_note: RECON test set of the CIA Suite: 500 human-annotated general-purpose instructions whose prompts were manually translated into six target languages (Bengali, German, French, Hindi, Telugu, Urdu), with reference answers and rubrics in English; general-purpose evaluation suite, coded Other.

canonical_reference: Singh et al. (2024), IndicGenBench: A Multilingual Benchmark to Evaluate Generation Capabilities of LLMs on Indic Languages. ACL 2024. arXiv:2404.16816.
languages: Assamese; Awadhi; Bengali; Bhojpuri; Bodo; Chhattisgarhi; Garhwali; Gujarati; Haryanvi; Hindi; Kannada; Konkani; Maithili; Malayalam; Manipuri; Marathi; Marwari; Nepali; Odia; Pashto; Punjabi; Rajasthani; Sanskrit; Santali; Tamil; Telugu; Tibetan; Urdu
evidence_note: Generation benchmark (cross-lingual summarization, machine translation, cross-lingual and multilingual QA) across 29 Indic languages, built mainly by collecting professional human translations of English source examples; the source divides its languages into higher (9), medium (7) and low (13) resource groups, so no single tier coded; multi-task generation suite, coded Other.

canonical_reference: Kim, Russell, Karpinska & Iyyer (2025), One Ruler to Measure Them All: Benchmarking Multilingual Long-Context Language Models. COLM 2025. arXiv:2503.01996.
evidence_note: Multilingual long-context benchmark adapting the English RULER benchmark across 26 languages: English instructions written first, then translated with native speakers into 25 further languages; seven synthetic retrieval and aggregation tasks, coded Other (long-context).

canonical_reference: Enevoldsen et al. (2025), MMTEB: Massive Multilingual Text Embedding Benchmark. ICLR 2025. arXiv:2502.13595.
evidence_note: Community expansion of MTEB aggregating 500+ existing embedding evaluation tasks; machine-translated datasets were removed during benchmark selection while constituent datasets include both originally authored and translated/bitext resources, so origin coded Mixed; language coverage is reported inconsistently by scope (250+ vs 1,000+ languages), so languages and count left undetermined; embedding benchmark, coded Other.

canonical_reference: Adelani et al. (2024), IrokoBench: A New Benchmark for African Languages in the Age of Large Language Models. arXiv:2406.03368.
evidence_note: Human-translated benchmark for 17 typologically diverse low-resource African languages covering NLI (AfriXNLI), mathematical reasoning (AfriMGSM) and multiple-choice knowledge QA (AfriMMLU) translated from English benchmarks; multi-task, coded Other; the abstract's language count differs between paper versions (16 vs 17).

canonical_reference: Asai et al. (2023), BUFFET: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Few-shot Cross-lingual Transfer. arXiv:2305.14857.
evidence_note: Unifies 15 existing datasets across 54 languages in a fixed few-shot format; the paper's curation table shows constituent datasets were curated by translation, in-language annotation and automatic alignment, so origin coded Mixed; multi-task suite, coded Other.
